title: Proof-of-Readiness Rubric for Enterprise Hosted API Feature Requests (chat / streaming / tool-calls / structured output)
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a lightweight, actionable "proof-of-readiness" rubric that product, sales, and solutions teams can apply to incoming feature requests for the Hosted API (particularly chat, streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs). The rubric will surface technical risk, cost delta, compliance blockers, and go/no-go routing for self-serve vs sales-assisted vs enterprise onboarding. This ticket drives a canonical decision checklist, a weighted scoring model to use in the intake form, and implementation notes for the Intake Pipeline (triage service).

Context: We continue to see high-volume, nuanced requests from enterprise customers that look similar on the surface but vary dramatically in SLO, data residency, encryption, and long-tail cost. Current intake signals are inconsistent across Sales and Solutions, which creates churn and slow onboarding. The rubric should help standardize decisions, reduce back-and-forth, and ensure requests are routed with the right support/commitment level.

Scope: 1) Rubric document with scoring weights and cutoffs. 2) Example decision flows for common request archetypes (streaming-only, chat+toolchain, webhook-heavy structured outputs). 3) Templates for intake responses (self-serve guidance, sales-assist checklist, enterprise engagement playbook). 4) A small prototype scoring widget spec for the intake UI (web). Not in scope: backend enforcement, billing automation (follow-ups will own these).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical rubric doc created and reviewed by Eng, Security, and Sales (link in 'links')
Scoring model with explicit weights for: latency sensitivity, throughput, expected QPS, required retention/residency, PII classification, SLO uplift, revenue potential
Three archetype decision flows (self-serve, sales-assisted, enterprise-onboard) with concrete next-step actions and owner assignments
Intake form wireframe + JSON schema for the scoring inputs
Stakeholder sign-off: PM, Solutions Eng, Sales AE, Security

rubric_summary: Signals captured: customer_size, expected_QPS, latency_SLO, retention_requirement, PII_flag, structured_output_complexity, tool_call_volume, revenue_urgency, runtime_impact, compliance_needs
Weight proposal (initial): latency_SLO=25, expected_QPS/cost=20, compliance/PII=20, strategic_value/revenue=15, implementation_complexity=10, runtime_impact=10 (normalized to 100)

Routing cutoffs (example): score < 30 -> self-serve (provide docs & cost estimate); 30-60 -> sales-assisted (Solutions Eng triage); > 60 or any compliance gate -> enterprise-onboard (assign Solutions Eng + Legal + Security)
Hard gates: PII_flag=true OR data_residency!='global' => enterprise-onboard mandatory

Fallback policy: If runtime_impact indicates 'kernel changes' or 'new quantization path' required, mark request 'Blocked' for engineering roadmap review and offer short-term model fallback suggestions
